name: Ngom
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.note: No description of Ngom (nra) located; only Grollemund 2012 comparative wordlist material cited on Glottolog

new_statements.quote: La longueur vocalique est notée au moyen d'un redoublement de la voyelle. Certains faits linguistiques qui nous sont apparues prévisibles, comme la nasalisation des voyelles orales devant des consonnes nasales, ou bien l'allongement des voyelles initiales de thèmes (V1) qui sont situées dans des syllabes accentuées, n'ont pas été pris en compte de manière systématique. [...] Pour simplifier la lecture, nous avons choisi de ne noter que le ton haut et les tons modulés (descendant et montant). L'absence de ton sur une syllabe correspond à la présence d'un ton bas sur cette même syllabe.
new_statements.translation: Vowel length is noted by doubling the vowel. Certain linguistic facts that appeared predictable to us, such as the nasalisation of oral vowels before nasal consonants, or the lengthening of stem-initial vowels (V1) that are located in accented syllables, have not been taken into account systematically. [...] To simplify reading, we chose to mark only the high tone and the contour tones (falling and rising). The absence of a tone mark on a syllable corresponds to the presence of a low tone on that syllable.
new_statements.citation: UNESCO Office Libreville / Université Omar Bongo, Laboratoire Universitaire de la Tradition Orale (LUTO) [Pither Medjo Mvé & Guy-Max Moussavou]. 2006. Lexique du kóya: langue des Pygmées du Nord-Est du Gabon. Libreville: UNESCO. §4.4 'Notation du lexique'.
new_statements.locator: §4.4 Notation du lexique, printed p. 20 (PDF page 25); page image verified (scanned/)
new_statements.reading: tone language with a stress statement
new_statements.rule_in_words: Koya (the Bakoya variety of Ungom/Ngom B22b) is a two-tone language (H vs L, plus rising and falling contours and a downstepped H). The only statement about accent is a passing one in the notation conventions: the stem-initial vowel (V1) sits in an 'accented syllable' and is predictably lengthened there, i.e. word-level prominence (with vowel lengthening) falls on the first syllable of the stem, after the noun-class prefix. This matches the stem-initial accent / C-emphasis pattern reported for north-western Bantu, but the source does not analyse it further.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated; the authors say the lengthening was not marked systematically and that tone of some prefixes/stems varies between singular and plural for unexplained 'intonosyntaxic' reasons; a detailed phonological study is deferred.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level, citation forms in a lexicon (singular/plural nouns and infinitives); 'thème' = stem after the class prefix. Describes Koya, not the Bungom (uŋgɔm) variety proper, though the source treats the two as one language (p. 10: 'la même langue'; 89.5% shared on 88 items).
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted source describes Koya (kóyà), the speech of the Bakoya ('Bakola') hunter-gatherers of Mékambo (Zadié, Ogooué-Ivindo), which it treats as a variety of Ungom/Ngom B22b ('le kóya est donc une variété de l'ungom', p. 10; 89.5% shared on 88 items; Nguéma Nkoghe 2004 gives 95.5%). Glottolog 5.3 has no separate dialect node under ngom1270; Grollemund's lexibank codes Koya as B22b_Koya under ngom1270; Koumbi Mabiti 2025 labels it B22c/B22e and UNESCO 2006 proposes B221. The Bungom (uŋgɔm) variety proper is described only in inaccessible sources (Maganga 2005; Mokrani 2016 relayed by Koumbi Mabiti 2025, tones only).

sources.note: §4.4 Notation du lexique, p. 20: two-tone notation (only H and rising/falling contours marked, unmarked = L; downstep marked); predictable 'allongement des voyelles initiales de thèmes (V1) qui sont situées dans des syllabes accentuées' left unmarked, i.e. stem-initial V1 sits in an accented syllable and is lengthened there. p. 10: koya = a variety of ungom (B22b); p. 16: only phonological descriptions are Nguema Nkoghe 2004 (koya) and Maganga 2005 (uŋgɔm), both UOB mémoires.

sources.note: §I.2.3.2 Uŋgɔm (B22b), pp. 102-106, data relayed from Mokrani 2016: 7 vowels, 19 consonants, 'un système simple de deux tons simples et de deux tons modulés' (H, B, montant, descendant); nothing on stress. §I.2.3.3 Koya p. 106 fn. 26: 'Sur le plan tonal, on note l'absence d'un traitement.' p. 237 (B20-wide diachrony): loss of H in stem T2 'pourrait conforter... une évolution vers un processus accentuel' (after Rekanga 2007, Dodo-Bouguendza 2010).

sources.note: pp. 41-42: ngom nord and ngom sud dissyllabic nominal tone reflexes (isolation forms from Jacquot 1983): ngom nord *BB > B-HB, *BH > B-HB, *HB > H-HB, *HH > H-HB; 'kele et ngom B-HB' for *BH; rightward spread of an initial H across B20. Tone only; no stress statement.
